issues.legal_issue: The right to defend property does not justify using deadly force against an unarmed trespasser who poses no threat of death or grievous hurt.
material_facts: The deceased entered the shop during a dispute over construction of a partition wall, and the court considered it likely that he was committing criminal trespass.
The court found no justification for concluding that the deceased was armed or intended to injure the appellant or his brother-in-law.

The appellant used a knife to inflict two fatal wounds to the deceased’s chest, although the circumstances did not create an apprehension that death or grievous hurt would be caused to the appellant or his brother-in-law.
issues.conclusion: The appellant had a right to remove the deceased from the shop, but exceeded his right of private defence of property by using the knife with deadly effect.
issues.legal_principle: A person may use force to remove a trespasser from property, but the court held that deadly force exceeded that right in the circumstances found here, where the trespasser was unarmed and posed no threat of death or grievous hurt. The judgment refers to Sections 302 and 304(1) of the Indian Penal Code in setting out the conviction and its replacement; it relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: murder_appeal and property_trespass and intruder_unarmed and no_threat_of_death_or_grievous_hurt and deadly_force_used

predicates.murder_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction for murder.
predicates.property_trespass: The deceased entered property in circumstances the court found amounted to criminal trespass.
predicates.intruder_unarmed: The court found no basis to conclude that the deceased was armed.
predicates.no_threat_of_death_or_grievous_hurt: The court found no apprehension that the deceased would cause death or grievous hurt to the accused or another person being defended.
predicates.deadly_force_used: The accused used a dangerous weapon with deadly effect against the trespasser.

issues.definition: When a murder appeal involves a trespasser who is unarmed and poses no threat of death or grievous hurt, using deadly force to defend property means the right of private defence has been exceeded.

issues.legal_issue: A killing committed while exceeding the right of private defence of property in circumstances that do not create an apprehension of death or grievous hurt does not sustain a murder conviction on the facts found.
material_facts: The deceased entered the shop in circumstances the court considered likely to amount to criminal trespass, but was not shown to be armed or to intend injury.
The appellant inflicted two fatal knife wounds to the deceased’s chest.
The court found that the appellant had no reason to apprehend that death or grievous hurt would be caused to him or his brother-in-law, and that he exceeded his right of private defence of property.
issues.conclusion: The murder conviction and life sentence could not be sustained. The appellant was convicted of culpable homicide under Section 304(1) of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to five years’ imprisonment.
issues.legal_principle: The court treated the fatal use of a dangerous weapon in excess of the right of private defence of property, where there was no apprehension of death or grievous hurt, as warranting conviction under Section 304(1) rather than Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: murder_appeal and fatal_stabbing and property_defence_context and no_threat_of_death_or_grievous_hurt and deadly_force_exceeded

predicates.murder_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction for murder.
predicates.fatal_stabbing: The accused inflicted knife wounds that caused the victim’s death.
predicates.property_defence_context: The accused used force in circumstances involving the victim’s entry onto property and a dispute over its use.
predicates.no_threat_of_death_or_grievous_hurt: The court found no apprehension that the victim would cause death or grievous hurt to the accused or another person being defended.
predicates.deadly_force_exceeded: The accused used deadly force beyond what was justified to defend the property.

issues.definition: Where a murder appeal concerns a fatal stabbing in a property-defence context, and the deadly force exceeded the right of defence without a threat of death or grievous hurt, the murder conviction is reduced to culpable homicide.
